entities.name: Neurocysticercosis
entities.description: A central nervous system parasitic infection caused by the larval metacestode stage (cysticerci) of the pork tapeworm Taenia solium, representing the leading identifiable cause of acquired adult-onset epilepsy in endemic regions worldwide.

entities.name: Ingestion of Taenia solium Eggs via Fecal-Oral Route
entities.description: Primary mode of transmission occurring exclusively through ingestion of microscopic Taenia solium eggs excreted in human tapeworm carrier feces via contaminated food, drinking water, unwashed agricultural produce, or fecal-oral autoinfection (consuming pork causes intestinal taeniasis, NOT neurocysticercosis).

entities.name: Household Contact with a Human Taenia solium Tapeworm Carrier
entities.description: Close contact, cohabitation, or food preparation by an individual harboring an adult intestinal Taenia solium tapeworm, acting as the direct source of infectious egg shedding.

entities.name: Residence in or Travel to Taenia solium Endemic Regions
entities.description: Living in or travel history to endemic regions of Latin America, South and Southeast Asia, or sub-Saharan Africa where inadequate sanitation, open human defecation, and free-roaming domestic swine perpetuate the life cycle.

entities.name: Subsistence Pig Farming with Free-Roaming Swine and Inadequate Sanitation
entities.description: Agro-environmental exposure in rural agricultural communities characterized by free-roaming domestic pigs accessing human feces and lack of sanitary latrines or meat inspection.

entities.name: Taenia solium Metacestode Larvae (Cysticercus cellulosae)
entities.description: The larval metacestode form of the cyclophyllidean pork tapeworm Taenia solium, establishing fluid-filled cystic structures within the cerebral parenchyma, subarachnoid spaces, or ventricular system after hematogenous oncosphere dissemination.

entities.name: New-Onset Adult Seizures in Endemic Setting
entities.description: Adult-onset focal seizures (with or without secondary generalization) or generalized tonic-clonic convulsions occurring in 70-90% of symptomatic parenchymal NCC, provoked either by active colloidal inflammatory edema or chronic epileptogenic gliotic calcified scars.

entities.name: Cystic Brain Lesion with Pathognomonic Invaginated Scolex on Neuroimaging
entities.description: Del Brutto absolute pathognomonic neuroimaging hallmark: a well-circumscribed 5-20 mm rounded cystic lesion containing an eccentric, punctate hyperdense or hyperintense mural nodule representing the invaginated scolex ('hole-with-a-dot' sign) on contrast CT or MRI.

entities.name: Bruns Syndrome Paroxysms from Mobile Intraventricular Cyst
entities.description: Paroxysmal, catastrophic attacks of severe occipital headache, projectile vomiting, vertiginous ataxia, and episodic syncope triggered by rotational head movements, caused by a mobile 4th ventricular cyst transiently occluding CSF outflow (ball-valve effect).

entities.name: Chronic Tension or Throbbing Headaches with Intracranial Hypertension
entities.description: Persistent severe headaches present in 35-50% of symptomatic patients, frequently associated with intracranial hypertension, nausea, vomiting, or papilledema due to hydrocephalus or basilar arachnoiditis.

entities.name: Colloidal Vesicular Stage Ring-Enhancing Lesion with Perilesional Edema
entities.description: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI finding showing round, ring-enhancing cystic lesions with thick regular capsular enhancement and marked surrounding hypodense vasogenic edema on T2/FLAIR, marking the host inflammatory attack against degenerating larvae.

entities.name: Punctate Calcified Granulomas on Non-Contrast Brain CT
entities.description: Non-contrast CT finding demonstrating single or multiple small (2-5 mm), discrete, hyperdense, non-enhancing punctate calcifications without active surrounding edema, representing non-viable mineralized parasitic remnants.

entities.name: Enzyme-Linked Immunoelectrotransfer Blot (EITB) Glycoprotein Antigen Seropositivity
entities.description: Gold-standard serological Western blot using lentil lectin-purified Taenia solium glycoprotein antigens (LL-GP), achieving >98% sensitivity and 100% specificity for patients with two or more viable parenchymal or extraparenchymal cysts.

entities.name: Racemose Subarachnoid Giant Lobulated Cystic Clusters in Basal Cisterns
entities.description: High-resolution neuroimaging (CISS/FIESTA MRI) revealing multilocular, grape-like budding cystic clusters within basal cisterns or Sylvian fissures without visible scolices, producing chronic basilar arachnoiditis, hydrocephalus, or stroke.

entities.name: CSF Lymphocytic Pleocytosis with Elevated Protein and Normal Glucose
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid profile in extraparenchymal or meningeal disease demonstrating 10-300 mononuclear cells/μL, elevated protein (50-300 mg/dL), normal to mildly decreased glucose, and elevated opening pressure.

entities.name: Normal Peripheral Leukocyte Count with Variable Mild Eosinophilia
entities.description: Standard CBC triage profile in parenchymal NCC characterized by normal total leukocyte count and absence of systemic leukocytosis; mild peripheral eosinophilia (5-10%) occurs in under 20-30% of cases and its absence does not rule out the disease.

entities.name: Acute Toxic High Spiking Fever with Meningismus and Purulent CSF Pleocytosis
entities.description: Acute high spiking fever, systemic toxic delirium, prominent meningeal rigidity, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis, and purulent turbid CSF pleocytosis, which rule out uncomplicated parenchymal neurocysticercosis.

entities.name: Restricted Diffusion on Diffusion-Weighted MRI (DWI) with Low ADC
entities.description: Central hyperintense restricted diffusion on DWI with corresponding hypointensity on apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping within a ring-enhancing brain mass, which rules out neurocysticercosis and confirms pyogenic bacterial abscess.

entities.name: Large Multilocular Cystic Lesions with Internal Daughter Cysts and Hydatid Sand
entities.description: Massive unilocular or multilocular intracranial cysts exhibiting internal daughter cysts, floating membranes ('water lily' sign), or hydatid sand, which rule out neurocysticercosis and establish cerebral echinococcosis.

entities.name: Irregular Shaggy Enhancing Infiltrative Cerebral Mass with Extensive Midline Shift
entities.description: Thick, irregular, nodular, shaggy enhancing margins with central necrosis, invasive parenchymal neovascularization, and severe midline shift, which rule out benign discrete neurocysticercosis cysts in favor of high-grade glioma or metastatic malignancy.

entities.name: Absence of Neuroimaging Lesions on Contrast Brain CT and High-Resolution MRI
entities.description: Complete absence of cystic lesions, mural nodules, ring enhancement, focal edema, or punctate calcifications on modern contrast-enhanced neuroimaging, which rules out active or inactive symptomatic neurocysticercosis.

entities.name: Cerebral Tuberculoma
entities.description: Intracranial granulomatous infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis presenting as ring-enhancing cerebral masses; differentiated from NCC by thick irregular nodular walls, T2-hypointense center, constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), pulmonary lesions, and negative Taenia solium EITB.

entities.name: Pyogenic Brain Abscess
entities.description: Bacterial intracranial focal infection causing ring-enhancing lesions; differentiated from NCC by acute high fever, toxic delirium, marked peripheral neutrophilia, elevated ESR/CRP, and hallmark central restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI/ADC).

entities.name: High-Grade Glioma and Brain Metastases
entities.description: Primary or secondary central nervous system malignancies presenting as ring-enhancing lesions; differentiated from NCC by thick shaggy irregular margins, central necrosis, progressive neurological deterioration, lack of discrete cystic walls, and absence of an eccentric scolex.

entities.name: Cerebral Echinococcosis
entities.description: Larval cestode infection caused by Echinococcus granulosus or multilocularis; differentiated from NCC by large expansive cysts containing internal daughter cysts and detached germinal membranes ('water lily' sign) rather than small scolex-containing cysts.

entities.name: Pre-Treatment High-Dose Corticosteroids (Dexamethasone or Prednisone)
entities.description: High-dose systemic corticosteroid therapy (dexamethasone 0.1 mg/kg/day or prednisone 1 mg/kg/day) initiated 24-48 hours prior to cysticidal anthelmintics to prevent life-threatening inflammatory cerebral edema, intracranial hypertension, and status epilepticus triggered by antigen release from dying cysticerci.

entities.name: Oral Albendazole Anthelmintic Therapy with Fatty Meals
entities.description: First-line cysticidal regimen of oral Albendazole (15 mg/kg/day divided twice daily for 10-14 days administered with fatty meals to maximize systemic absorption and CSF penetration) achieving parasiticidal destruction of 1-2 viable parenchymal cysts.

entities.name: Dual Anthelmintic Regimen with Albendazole and Praziquantel
entities.description: Combination therapy of oral Albendazole (15 mg/kg/day) plus oral Praziquantel (50 mg/kg/day divided 3 times daily) for 10-14 days, achieving significantly superior cyst clearance (>75% resolution) compared to monotherapy in patients with multiple (>2) viable parenchymal cysts.

entities.name: Anti-Epileptic Drug Monotherapy for Seizure Control
entities.description: First-line anti-epileptic monotherapy (e.g., levetiracetam, carbamazepine) providing effective seizure prophylaxis for acute provoked seizures during inflammatory degeneration and as the sole indicated treatment for inactive calcified epileptogenic lesions.

entities.name: Anthelmintic Cysticidal Therapy in Inactive Calcified Lesions Alone
entities.description: Inactive calcified granulomas contain only dead, mineralized parasitic debris and are intrinsically unresponsive to anthelmintic therapy; cysticidal drugs are contraindicated as they provide no clinical benefit and carry risks of unnecessary adverse effects.

entities.name: Anthelmintic Therapy in Untreated Hydrocephalus or Cysticercal Encephalitis
entities.description: Administration of cysticidal drugs is contraindicated in untreated obstructive hydrocephalus or massive cysticercal encephalitis because acute parasite lysis precipitates fatal intracranial hypertension and herniation; primary management requires surgical CSF diversion and high-dose anti-inflammatory agents.

relationships.target: Ingestion of Taenia solium Eggs via Fecal-Oral Route
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Acquired exclusively through the fecal-oral ingestion of microscopic Taenia solium eggs shed in the feces of a human tapeworm carrier via contaminated food, water, or poor hygiene; consuming pork causes intestinal taeniasis, NOT neurocysticercosis.

relationships.target: Household Contact with a Human Taenia solium Tapeworm Carrier
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Clustered risk resulting from household cohabitation or close personal contact with an individual harboring an adult intestinal tapeworm shedding infective eggs.

relationships.target: Residence in or Travel to Taenia solium Endemic Regions
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Epidemiological exposure in endemic rural regions of Latin America, South/Southeast Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa where the domestic pig-human transmission cycle remains active.

relationships.target: Subsistence Pig Farming with Free-Roaming Swine and Inadequate Sanitation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Environmental exposure in agricultural settings where free-roaming domestic pigs feed on human feces due to lack of closed latrines and sanitation infrastructure.

relationships.target: Taenia solium Metacestode Larvae (Cysticercus cellulosae)
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by the larval metacestode stage (cysticerci) of Taenia solium colonizing the brain parenchyma, ventricular cavities, or subarachnoid spaces.

relationships.target: New-Onset Adult Seizures in Endemic Setting
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Adult-onset focal or generalized tonic-clonic seizures in an endemic area represent the primary cardinal clinical presentation (70-90% of symptomatic parenchymal cases), triggered by colloidal host inflammation or chronic calcified scars.

relationships.target: Cystic Brain Lesion with Pathognomonic Invaginated Scolex on Neuroimaging
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Del Brutto absolute diagnostic criterion defined by a 5-20 mm cystic lesion with an eccentric hyperdense or hyperintense mural nodule representing the invaginated scolex ('hole-with-a-dot' sign) on CT or MRI.

relationships.target: Bruns Syndrome Paroxysms from Mobile Intraventricular Cyst
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Episodic severe occipital headache, projectile vomiting, and syncope provoked by head rotation due to intermittent obstruction of CSF flow by a mobile 4th ventricular cyst via a ball-valve mechanism.

relationships.target: Chronic Tension or Throbbing Headaches with Intracranial Hypertension
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Persistent severe headaches presenting in 35-50% of symptomatic patients, often accompanied by vomiting, visual obscurations, or papilledema due to hydrocephalus or basilar inflammation.

relationships.target: Colloidal Vesicular Stage Ring-Enhancing Lesion with Perilesional Edema
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Neuroimaging pattern on contrast CT/MRI displaying smooth, round ring-enhancing parenchymal cysts with capsule enhancement and prominent perilesional vasogenic edema on T2/FLAIR reflecting active host immune response.

relationships.target: Punctate Calcified Granulomas on Non-Contrast Brain CT
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission non-contrast CT pattern showing single or multiple 2-5 mm discrete hyperdense non-enhancing calcified nodules devoid of edema, indicating chronic non-viable mineralized parasitic scars.

relationships.target: Enzyme-Linked Immunoelectrotransfer Blot (EITB) Glycoprotein Antigen Seropositivity
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum/CSF Western blot utilizing lentil lectin-purified Taenia solium glycoprotein antigens (LL-GP) showing >98% sensitivity and 100% specificity in patients with multiple viable or extraparenchymal cysts.

relationships.target: Racemose Subarachnoid Giant Lobulated Cystic Clusters in Basal Cisterns
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Multilocular, grape-like budding cystic clusters within basal cisterns or Sylvian fissures lacking scolices, causing basilar arachnoiditis, hydrocephalus, or endarteritis obliterans leading to stroke.

relationships.target: CSF Lymphocytic Pleocytosis with Elevated Protein and Normal Glucose
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Cerebrospinal fluid pattern in extraparenchymal disease demonstrating lymphocytic pleocytosis (10-300 WBC/μL), elevated protein (50-300 mg/dL), normal or mildly decreased glucose, and elevated opening pressure.

relationships.target: Normal Peripheral Leukocyte Count with Variable Mild Eosinophilia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Complete blood count profile at admission triage showing normal total WBC count without neutrophilic leukocytosis; mild peripheral eosinophilia occurs in <20-30% of cases and its absence does not rule out NCC.

relationships.target: Acute Toxic High Spiking Fever with Meningismus and Purulent CSF Pleocytosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of acute high fever, toxic encephalopathy, nuchal rigidity, marked peripheral leukocytosis, and turbid purulent CSF pleocytosis rules out uncomplicated parenchymal neurocysticercosis, indicating acute bacterial meningitis or brain abscess.

relationships.target: Restricted Diffusion on Diffusion-Weighted MRI (DWI) with Low ADC
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Central hyperintense signal on DWI with low ADC mapping within a cystic ring-enhancing lesion rules out neurocysticercosis, confirming a pyogenic bacterial brain abscess.

relationships.target: Large Multilocular Cystic Lesions with Internal Daughter Cysts and Hydatid Sand
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Finding of expansive, large multivesicular cysts containing internal daughter cysts or hydatid sand rules out neurocysticercosis, establishing cerebral echinococcosis.

relationships.target: Irregular Shaggy Enhancing Infiltrative Cerebral Mass with Extensive Midline Shift
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Grossly irregular, thick, shaggy enhancing margins with central necrosis, invasive parenchymal infiltrative edema, and rapid mass effect rule out discrete benign neurocysticercosis cysts, indicating glioblastoma or brain metastasis.

relationships.target: Absence of Neuroimaging Lesions on Contrast Brain CT and High-Resolution MRI
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of cystic lesions, mural nodules, ring enhancement, focal edema, or calcifications on dedicated high-resolution contrast brain imaging rules out active or inactive symptomatic neurocysticercosis.

relationships.target: Cerebral Tuberculoma
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cerebral Tuberculoma: Tuberculomas display thick irregular nodular rim enhancement with central T2-hypointensity, systemic constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), chest X-ray findings, and negative EITB, whereas NCC lesions are smooth, afebrile, and EITB positive.

relationships.target: Pyogenic Brain Abscess
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Pyogenic Brain Abscess: Pyogenic abscess presents with acute toxic high fever, marked peripheral neutrophilia, elevated ESR/CRP, and central restricted diffusion on DWI/ADC, whereas parenchymal NCC lacks systemic toxemia, has normal inflammatory labs, and shows non-restricting cyst fluid.

relationships.target: High-Grade Glioma and Brain Metastases
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from High-Grade Glioma and Brain Metastases: Neoplastic brain lesions exhibit thick, nodular, irregular enhancing margins with central necrosis, invasive parenchymal distortion, and progressive clinical deterioration, contrasting with the discrete, non-infiltrative, stage-specific morphology of neurocysticercosis.

relationships.target: Cerebral Echinococcosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cerebral Echinococcosis: Echinococcus granulosus or multilocularis presents as huge unilocular or multilocular mass lesions often containing internal daughter cysts without perilesional edema prior to rupture, lacking the pathognomonic invaginated scolex dot of Taenia solium.

relationships.target: Pre-Treatment High-Dose Corticosteroids (Dexamethasone or Prednisone)
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] High-dose corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.1 mg/kg/day or prednisone 1 mg/kg/day) administered 24-48 hours before cysticidal anthelmintic therapy prevent severe local parenchymal inflammatory edema, intracranial hypertension, and status epilepticus triggered by parasitic antigen release.

relationships.target: Oral Albendazole Anthelmintic Therapy with Fatty Meals
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Oral Albendazole (15 mg/kg/day divided twice daily for 10-14 days taken with fat-containing meals to optimize systemic bioavailability) achieves successful parasiticidal destruction of 1-2 viable parenchymal cysticerci.

relationships.target: Dual Anthelmintic Regimen with Albendazole and Praziquantel
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Combined Albendazole (15 mg/kg/day) plus Praziquantel (50 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses) for 10-14 days achieves significantly higher cyst resolution rates (>75%) than monotherapy in patients with multiple (>2) viable parenchymal cysts.

relationships.target: Anti-Epileptic Drug Monotherapy for Seizure Control
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] First-line anti-epileptic monotherapy (levetiracetam, carbamazepine) provides effective seizure suppression in both active inflammatory and inactive calcified parenchymal disease.

relationships.target: Anthelmintic Cysticidal Therapy in Inactive Calcified Lesions Alone
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Dead, mineralized calcified parenchymal lesions contain no living metacestodes and are intrinsically unresponsive to anthelmintics (albendazole/praziquantel); cysticidal therapy is contraindicated as it confers no clinical benefit and causes drug-induced adverse effects.

relationships.target: Anthelmintic Therapy in Untreated Hydrocephalus or Cysticercal Encephalitis
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Cysticidal anthelmintics are contraindicated prior to surgical CSF diversion in hydrocephalus or in massive cysticercal encephalitis because drug-induced larval lysis precipitates fatal intracranial hypertension and herniation; therapy requires initial neurosurgical decompression and anti-inflammatory management.
